title: Fiscal series
description:
External economic series that pay-regime rules are denominated in. Kept as its own document type, alongside regimes and crosswalks, for the same reason: a regime states what a law says, and must not carry statistics that get revised underneath it.

This exists because the draft law is not self-contained. Art. 9(4) bounds the reference value by nominal GDP growth; Art. 36(3) sets the uplift from 2028 by a target to cut the public wage bill by at least 1.5 points of GDP between 2024 and 2031; Art. 23(3)-(4) gates a local supplement on ratios of local tax revenue. None of those can be evaluated from the statute alone.

These series bound and denominate. They do not justify: a wage bill of x% of GDP says what a pay structure costs, never what any post ought to be paid.

methodology.description: The statistical standard, e.g. ESA 2010. Two series are only comparable across countries when this matches.

retrieved.description: Statistical agencies revise back series. The retrieval date is part of this document's identity, not metadata - a chart drawn today and one drawn last year can legitimately disagree.

query.description: Enough to re-derive the document from the publisher. Makes the import reproducible rather than merely repeatable.

id.description: Stable identifier a regime's cap can point at.

unit.description: PC_GDP is a share of GDP - a structural ratio, and therefore the only form in which Romanian and Danish figures may be shown side by side. Currency units must never be compared across the two. COUNT is a plain tally of things - institutions, posts, reporting units - and carries no currency, so it needs no such rule.

dims.description: Free-form classification. `family` optionally maps a COFOG function onto an occupational family in the regimes; that mapping is approximate and each document says so in limitations.

period.description: ISO year, or YYYY-MM for sub-annual.

value.description: null where the publisher reports no observation. Never interpolated: a gap is information.

flag.description: Publisher's flag, e.g. p for provisional, e for estimated.
